answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making every identity anchor itself to one costly, non-transferable work record: before trading, an agent locks a deposit and completes verified jobs that build a single public history. A newcomer starts with tiny quotas that grow only from that history, so a gale of fresh fake identities buys no trust at all, since each fake must pay its own deposit and do its own real work. Across the whole ocean of agents, copying an identity is useless because the record cannot be transferred, so attack cost scales with every fake while honest agents pay once.
